Sibuna v0.3.5 expands upstream distribution packages and installation documentation.
The five Linux/macOS/Windows binary archives retain their native qualification.
Request inspection, console behavior and storage schema retain their v0.3.3 contracts.
The embedded console source offer names this immutable v0.3.5 tag.

Downloads:
- Linux x86-64 and ARM64: static musl archives, Debian .deb and RPM .rpm.
- Arch Linux x86-64: sibuna-bin .pkg.tar.zst, installed with pacman -U.
- FreeBSD 15.1/amd64: native CLI .pkg, installed with pkg add.
- OpenBSD 7.9/amd64: native CLI .tgz, installed with pkg_add -D unsigned.
- macOS Apple Silicon and Intel: unsigned CLI archives; macOS 15 or later.
- Windows x86-64: native executable ZIP; Windows 10 / Server 2019 or later.
- Offline corresponding-source bundle with verified SQLite inputs.
- Source-built Homebrew formula (sibuna.rb), using Zig 0.17.0; no cask.
- Helm chart 0.3.5 and public ghcr.io/insanai/sibuna:0.3.5 image for amd64/arm64.

Verify SHA256SUMS before installing the exact package for your OS/CPU. These are
unsigned upstream artifacts, not acceptance into community archives or BSD ports.
The OpenBSD unsigned option is specific to the explicitly downloaded file and does
not disable signature verification in configured system repositories. Official
ports, signed APT/DNF/pacman repositories, AUR, Homebrew core, WinGet and GNU Guix
remain independent submission and qualification work. No existing tag is replaced.

Linux packages install a locked service account and optional stopped systemd unit.
Set the IP-literal origin in /etc/sibuna/service.env before explicitly enabling it.
The proxy defaults to 127.0.0.1:8080. Console setup is an operator decision.
Configuration, private admission seed, state and identity survive removal; upgrades
require explicit restart after backup and review.

BSD packages install only /usr/local/bin/sibuna and license/security/source notices.
They create no service, account, credentials or state. Run as an unprivileged user
with private seed/state and stop before package replacement/removal. FreeBSD rc.subr,
OpenBSD rc.d/rcctl and Linux systemd are separate; no BSD service or pledge/unveil
integration is claimed. Metadata names the native ABI/library requirements.

The English and seven translated READMEs, book, operator guide and website cover
all installation mechanisms, verification, upgrades and retained credentials/data.
The build-only source-map-js dependency is updated to 1.2.2 for GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q;
regenerated runtime CSS is byte-identical and this dependency is not in the daemon.
Startup initializes allocated incident and telemetry rings in place, avoiding temporaries
larger than OpenBSD's ordinary stack limit. Its C build omits the indirect-function
sanitizer that reads execute-only libc code; other safe checks and OS protections
remain enabled. Linux/macOS/Windows C flags are unchanged.
Paxos durable-state invariant validation iterates its stored window by pointer,
avoiding large nested stack copies during retained journal replay.
WebSocket test fixtures mask large frames efficiently under software emulation,
with independent RFC frame checks and the original daemon idle deadlines retained.

Publication requires all native executable/CRS gates, Linux package/systemd
lifecycles, both BSD native builds and installed unprivileged runtime/replace/remove
checks, the Homebrew source build/test, and the minimal container/Restricted
Kubernetes install/upgrade/uninstall tests. IMAGE-DIGEST.txt names the anonymously
accessible multi-platform image. The container carries CA certificates and identity
data, with no shell, compiler, package manager or download utilities. Helm retains
the operator-owned Secret and single-writer PVC; qualify production CNI/ingress.

Upgrade:
- Console schema remains 46; no migration is introduced.
- Preserve admission seed, console key and state; back up before upgrading.
- Before v0.3.2, upgrade every cluster node: older binaries cannot use schema 46.
- Package/Helm rollback does not undo a database migration.
- No measured request subsystem changed. The required primitive benchmark refresh
  records its source commit and shared-host conditions; earlier dated measurements
  retain their provenance. The SID 0007 console performance exception remains.

The engine is LGPL-3.0; the console and combined binary are AGPL-3.0. All packages
carry license texts, notices, security guidance and corresponding-source provenance.
Third-party materials retain their licenses. CRS rules are Apache-2.0, downloaded
and verified at runtime rather than bundled. Report vulnerabilities privately
through the repository's GitHub security reporting page.
